verdict: FAIL - three P0 pre-existing authorization defects block Phase 1 readiness

critical.title: PATCH /api/bookings/{booking} bypasses permission:bookings.edit
critical.proof: Runtime probe, not inference. A User with role 'user' and RolePermissionChecker::userHasPermission($u,'bookings.edit') === false issued PATCH /api/bookings/{id} with {'status':'approved','price':1} and received HTTP 200 'Booking updated successfully'. The persisted row afterwards had status='approved' and price=1.00.
critical.mechanism: Route::apiResource('bookings')->only([... 'update' ...]) registers BOTH PUT and PATCH for the same URI. The later, permission-gated Route::put('/bookings/{booking}') overrides only PUT in Laravel's per-method lookup table. PATCH therefore resolves to the apiResource route whose middleware is only ['api','auth:sanctum'].
amplifiers: BookingController::update validates 'status' => 'sometimes|string' with no Rule::in(...) constraint and 'price' => 'sometimes|numeric|min:0'.
Both 'status' and 'price' are in Booking::$fillable (lines 113 and 103).
RescheduleBookingUseCase line 135 performs $booking->update($validated) with the validated payload.
critical.impact: Any authenticated user can set any booking's status and price. That is unauthenticated-in-effect financial tampering and state-machine bypass, and it bypasses the payment and approval flows entirely.
critical.remediation_requires: Adding permission middleware to the PATCH verb, or restricting the accepted fields, or both. Either changes the external API contract and the authorization outcome, so it is NOT applied here - it needs explicit approval.

critical.title: 19 /api/v2/* routes are fully anonymous
critical.proof: php artisan route:list --json shows middleware ['api'] with no Authenticate entry for all 19.
critical.impact: Anonymous read of all payments, ledger and settlement data; anonymous write of settlement batches and booking state transitions.
critical.remediation_requires: Adding auth middleware changes the API contract (200 -> 401) and is not applied here.

critical.title: Role and partner administration have no permission middleware
critical.proof: route:list shows Authenticate:sanctum present but zero PermissionMiddleware entries for all /api/roles* and /api/partners* routes.
detail: PUT /api/roles/{role}/permissions - any authenticated user can grant permissions to any role, including their own. This is direct privilege escalation.

DELETE /api/partners/{partner}, POST /api/partners/{partner}/approve, POST /api/partners/{partner}/reject, POST /api/partners/{partner}/mark-under-review, GET /api/partners/kpis, GET /api/partners/{partner}/commissions, POST /api/partners/create-with-onboarding
critical.impact: Privilege escalation and unauthenticated-in-effect partner lifecycle control.
critical.remediation_requires: Permission middleware must be added per route, which changes authorization outcomes. Not applied here.

high.title: Gallery CRUD is fully anonymous
high.detail: GET/POST /api/gallery, GET/PUT|PATCH/DELETE /api/gallery/{gallery} all have middleware ['api'] only.

high.title: Admin bulk asset import endpoints are anonymous
high.detail: POST /api/admin/assets/import/confirm performs a bulk inventory write with middleware ['api'] only, despite the /admin/ prefix. Also anonymous: /api/admin/assets/import/template (GET), /api/admin/assets/import/validate (POST), POST /api/admin/screen-categories.

high.title: .env.testing contains real database credentials and is not git-ignored
high.detail: db_illuvision_testing credentials are committed in plaintext. If the repository is ever published, or if .env.testing is deployed, those credentials are exposed. It is not listed in .gitignore.

medium.title: Authenticated-but-unpermissioned uploads
medium.detail: POST /api/file-upload and POST /api/video-upload require only auth:sanctum, so any authenticated user can upload.

medium.title: Controller-internal authorization is inconsistent
medium.detail: Because middleware is the primary gate, any route with a missing or mis-scoped permission entry is unprotected. SEC-01, SEC-03, SEC-07 are all instances of this single root cause.

verified_clean.check: client-supplied money trusted on the campaign booking path
verified_clean.detail: CreateCampaignBookingUseCase derives authoritative subtotal/discount/final from CampaignPricingService; client subtotal/discount_amount/final_amount are informational only and never stored or charged.

CreatePaymentOrderUseCase derives the order amount from the persisted Payment record. PaymentController::verify accepts only razorpay_order_id, razorpay_payment_id and razorpay_signature - no amount field exists on the request, and the Razorpay signature covers order_id|payment_id.

No request input reaches DB::raw or string-concatenated SQL. The 3 interpolated DB::raw expressions (RewardReportQuery, RevenueAnalyticsService, RevenueDistributionService) interpolate hardcoded DB-driver literals only.
No model has an empty $fillable together with an empty $guarded.
The Phase 0.13 fix holds; now enforced by ArchitectureRuleTest::test_no_model_imports_the_http_layer.

all_findings_pre_existing: Every finding above was compared against docs/audit/routes-baseline.json, the pre-remediation snapshot. All appear with IDENTICAL middleware. Phases 0.5-0.14 neither introduced nor worsened any of them.
hard_stop_note: SEC-01, SEC-02 and SEC-03 are contract-changing remediations. The Phase 0.16 brief forbids changing authorization outcomes or the API contract as a side effect, so they are recorded as P0 blockers for explicit approval rather than silently fixed.
